subject: Request: Custom service commitment (availability & latency) — order form language and annex
messages:
From: Lara Chen <lara.chen@mediquip.com>
To: alex_martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@mediquip.com
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Service commitments: availability & P95 latency for enterprise order form

Hi Alex,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed with the latency profiles and the prefix cache demo. Before we advance to legal/procurement, procurement leadership has asked for a couple of specific commitments in writing that must be reflected in the Order Form and an MSA/SOW annex:

- Availability: target 99.99% monthly uptime, with clearly defined credit calculation if availability falls below 99.99.
- P95 inference latency (end-to-end, 1k token test profile): <= 250ms for dedicated pool with the proposed reserved capacity.
- Runbook & evidence: access to 30 days of per-route uptime/latency metrics and audit logs for quarterly reviews, and a SOC-type evidence bundle for procurement review.

We anticipate a kickoff for procurement redlines next week. Can you confirm whether Redwood can (1) commit to the 99.99 target for the Dedicated SKU we discussed, (2) provide suggested order form language and an annex that defines measurement windows and credit formulas, and (3) include the evidence bundle items?

Attaching a short PDF with their internal requirements (Mediquip_SLA_ask_v1.pdf).

Best,
Lara Chen
Sr. Procurement Manager
Mediquip

---
Attachment: Mediquip_SLA_ask_v1.pdf (1 page; procurement checklist)

From: alex.martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Lara Chen <lara.chen@mediquip.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 11:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service commitments: availability & P95 latency for enterprise order form

Hi Lara — thanks for the clear ask and the PDF. Quick answers up front:

1) Availability: We can propose a Dedicated-orderform annex that targets 99.99% availability for the reserved capacity configuration you outlined, with tiered credits (full credit schedule) for monthly windows below that target. We need product/infra sign-off on the exact credit caps for catastrophic events.
2) Latency: P95 <= 250ms is achievable for a dedicated pool with the runtime knobs we discussed (continuous batching tuned for 1k token profile + KV cache warm state). We will call out measurement method (synthetic p95 over 1k requests/day, 99th-percentile exclusion rules for scheduled maintenance).
3) Evidence: we can produce per-route latency/availability dashboards and an evidence package (audit logs + sample traces) for the last 30 days. SOC bundles are handled by security; I'll loop them in if you need raw artifacts.

I'll put together a proposed annex (order-form clause + credit formula + measurement windows) and circulate today. Marissa / Aditya — looping you for legal/redline and product/prod-eng review before I send to procurement.

Next step: Marissa, can you prepare the order form markup and a short credit schedule that maps to our standard Dedicated SLA policy? Aditya — can you confirm whether the proposed measurement script (1k token p95) is consistent with our perf harness and flag any caveats?

Thanks — Alex
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: OrderForm_Draft.pdf (draft order form we discussed)

From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: alex.martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, mina_haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: Draft annex & proposed credit formula for Mediquip — please review/redline

Alex / team,

Thanks — I attached a redline of the proposed annex (RDW_proposed-annex_v2.docx). High-level notes:

- Credit banding: I recommend capping monthly credit at 50% of one month's dedicated fee for availability breaches down to 99.5%. Below 98% escalates to executive review (we've used similar in other enterprise deals).
- Measurement window: Use calendar-month windows with a 5-minute monitoring granularity; exclude scheduled maintenance windows with 48h notification.
- Latency: Suggested language defines the measurement as "synthetic p95" measured from Redwood's telemetry on dedicated pool ingress to token completion, over a 24h rolling window, excluding network client-side anomalies identified by correlation traces. Add explicit warm-cache clause.
- Evidence: We can provide a daily export of per-route metrics (CSV), SOC evidence summary, and a secure link for quarterly audit exports. Security will not provide raw HSM keys but will provide KMS attestations.

Mina — legal will want tighter definitions around "scheduled maintenance" and "catastrophic events". Please flag anything unacceptable. Aditya — any performance caveats to call out to the customer (e.g., model size variance, cold-start penalties)?

I've kept the order form markup limited — primary changes are the SLA annex reference and the credit schedule table. If agreed, Alex please circulate to Lara + procurement with the annex as the proposed order-form attachment.

Marissa Cole
VP, Legal Operations
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: RDW_proposed-annex_v2.docx (redline, 3 pages)
Attachment: OrderForm_Draft.pdf

From: alex.martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Lara Chen <lara.chen@mediquip.com>, Mark Donovan <m.donovan@mediquip.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, mina_haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2027 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service commitments: availability & P95 latency for enterprise order form

Hi Lara / Mark — looping back with the proposed materials.

What we're sending you now:
- RDW_proposed-annex_v2.docx (redline with credit table and measurement definitions)
- OrderForm_Draft.pdf (annotated to reference the annex)
- A short attachment summarizing evidence types we can provide (OrderForm_Draft.pdf page 2)

Key callouts for Mediquip to review:
1) Availability target: 99.99% (proposed) with the credit schedule in the annex. Cap on monthly credits at 50% of that month's Dedicated fees for availability falls between 99.99% and 99.5% (see table).
2) Latency: P95 definition and synthetic measurement method are in section 2.2. We included a warm-cache clause and excluded client-network anomalies from measurement.
3) Evidence & audits: We will provide a daily per-route CSV export and a quarterly audit bundle; SOC-style artifacts summarized in the annex. For deeper audits we can coordinate an agreed data exchange procedure.

Next steps: Please review the redline and let us know any non-starters. If language looks good, procurement can confirm whether they need a higher credit cap or alternative remediation (e.g., termination right after consecutive breaches) — we can escalate to execs if needed.

If acceptable, can we get procurement confirmation on the redline by Tue 20 Jul so legal can produce a final clean annex for signature?

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
